segments.t: Defaults for the dual-panel KTPH001SFTP file managerKTPH002 and for the JobScheduler's Rsync jobs. Open via KTPH003Configuration → Global Settings → SFTP ManagerKTPH004; stored in KTPH000.

An idle SFTP tab closes itself after the timeout, which frees the server-side connection when you forget to close the manager. The timeout field is only editable while the toggle is on, and the two share one stored value: switching the toggle off stores no timeout at all. While uploads or downloads are running the tab counts as active, so it never closes itself in the middle of a transfer.
How uploads and downloads in the KTPH000transfer listKTPH001 work. Changes apply to SFTP tabs opened afterwards.
Ask (with "apply to all"), Skip the file, Overwrite
Keep the partial file when a transfer is cancelled

Each parallel transfer uses one SFTP channel of its own next to the one the tab browses with. Three channels give most of the speed on slow links and stay well below the usual server limit of ten sessions per connection; when the server refuses a channel, the tab quietly copies with fewer. A tab that borrows a terminal pane's session uses at most 2, whatever the setting says.

KTPH000AskKTPH001 shows the KTPH002file already existsKTPH003 dialog once per upload or download, with KTPH004Apply to allKTPH005. KTPH006Skip the fileKTPH007 and KTPH008OverwriteKTPH009 answer it without asking; folders are merged either way. KTPH010OverwriteKTPH011 never replaces a symbolic link, or a file where a folder is expected (and the other way round): those are still asked about.

Every transfer writes into a KTPH000 file next to its target first. With KTPH001Resume interrupted transfersKTPH002 on, a transfer that failed or lost its connection keeps that file, and KTPH003RetryKTPH004 continues where it stopped after checking that the source has not changed. Switched off, the partial file is removed whenever a transfer does not finish, and a retry starts from the beginning. KTPH005Keep the partial file when a transfer is cancelledKTPH006 also keeps it on KTPH007CancelKTPH008, so a cancelled transfer can be resumed too; it can only be switched on while resuming is on.

An organization can cap KTPH002Parallel transfersKTPH003 and set and lock KTPH004When the target already existsKTPH005 with KTPH006KTPH000KTPH007, and switch file transfer off entirely with KTPH001; the page then says so below the transfer settings.
The editor that KTPH000Edit in External EditorKTPH001 in the KTPH002SFTP file managerKTPH003 opens server files with.
A program and its arguments; KTPH000 stands for the file

Examples: KTPH000, KTPH001, KTPH002. Words are separated by spaces; put a path with spaces in double or single quotes. KTPH003 is replaced by the full path of the local copy as one argument, and without KTPH004 the path is added at the end. The command runs directly, never through a shell, so KTPH005, KTPH006, KTPH007 and KTPH008 have no special meaning. A command with an unclosed quote is marked red and not saved. Leave the field empty to open files as text with the system's editor: TextEdit (or your default text editor) on macOS, the KTPH009EditKTPH010 action (usually Notepad) on Windows, and on Linux the default application for text files; on Linux a file that is not plain text asks for an editor command first, which is then stored here.
These are the defaults for creating a ZIP archive KTPH000on the remote serverKTPH001 from the SFTP manager.
KTPH000 means no compression (fastest) and KTPH001 the best compression (slowest).

Leave the path empty to use the KTPH000 found on KTPH001. KTPH004BrowseKTPH005 picks a binary explicitly. Rsync jobs additionally require KTPH002 to be available on KTPH003; see KTPH006JobSchedulerKTPH007.
